card.intuition: Human review means reading the code the agent produced and judging it, which means reading the diff or the changed files. Reading the agent's description of what it did does not count, because narration is a secondary source written by the party being reviewed. Since agents raise the volume of code, review becomes the bottleneck, so it is reserved for what only you can judge and layered on top of automated checks and automated review.
card.analogy: Like auditing a contract: the lawyer's summary of the changes is not the deliverable; you read the redline of the actual agreement, because that is where the substance lives.
card.time_complexity: Operational cost rises the later review happens: a plan or a small mid-flight diff takes minutes, while excavating a finished branch after an AFK run takes far longer.
card.space_complexity: Context footprint is the reviewer's own: rebuilding the shape of a whole feature from a finished branch consumes far more working memory than following it step by step as it was built.
when_to_use: Deciding whether a change is the right change and whether it should exist at all
Checking whether an approach fits the codebase, not just whether it passes
As an early, cheap checkpoint: reviewing a plan or a small mid-flight diff rather than only end-of-branch excavation
gotchas: Reading the agent's summary is not review; the diff is the primary source
Agents raise code volume until review is the bottleneck, so it must be layered with automated checks and review
Treated as an afterthought, human review lands late at the most expensive point
